ben: Ran a trace-emulation sweep on the EU-prod traces today with a new batch formation heuristic (elastic-window) + token budget tuning. Quick summary and artifacts below.

ben: Command I used:
```
./tools/trace_emulator --trace=s3://redwood-traces/eu/2026-03-15.tgz \n  --batcher=elastic-window --token-budget=128 --queue-policy=delayed-assemble \n  --kernel-selection=auto --kv-prefetch=off --emit-profiles --out=s3://redwood-sim/trace-emu/1839123456/
```

alice: Nice. Where are the raw sim outputs + per-request kernel picks? want to diff against last week's run.

ben: s3://redwood-sim/trace-emu/1839123456/ — uploaded per_request_kernel.csv and a small summary.jsonl. CSV header looks like:
```
request_id,seq_len,chosen_kernel,kernel_latency_ms,kv_hit,queued_ms,batch_size
```

carol: did you enable KV warmup for that sweep? kv_warmup changes kernel choice distribution a lot.

ben: no, kv_prefetch=off explicitly to isolate batch formation impact. we'll run a separate sweep with warmup later.

dave: I ran an A/B in the emulator with two model variants (quantized-int8 vs float32). Observations: elastic-window tends to split long sessions into more sub-batches which increases effective kernel-switch overhead. On A100s the selector preferred int8-gemm for many mid-length sequences. profiling snippet (p95 lat):
```
variant,token_budget,p95_latency_ms,throughput_rps
float32,128,420,118
int8,128,390,115
int8,64,360,110
```

infra-bot: [sim-job-complete] job_id=emu-1839123456 status=SUCCESS duration=2h12m metrics={p50: 28ms, p95: 380ms, p99: 820ms, throughput: 115rps} artifacts: per_request_kernel.csv, profiles.tar.gz

alice: we saw a regression in p99 for short queries when token_budget=128. suspect queueing delays for small messages. can you test token_budget=64? might improve tail.

ben: ran token_budget=64 (same trace subset). Results: p50 basically unchanged, p95 -30ms, p99 -120ms, throughput -4%. quick diff table:
```
metric,128,64,delta
p50,26ms,26ms,0
p95,410ms,380ms,-30ms
p99,940ms,820ms,-120ms
throughput,119rps,114rps,-5rps (-4%)
```

carol: interesting. also noticed kernel selector sometimes picks int8 even when KV miss penalty pushes total end-to-end above float path. our cost model needs a warmup/miss penalty term.

dave: also saw many tiny incomplete batches because delayed-assemble max_delay was 10ms. lowering to 6ms reduced small-batch tail but slightly increased token-aggregation loss on medium requests.

alice: @ben can you add the 64-run + altered-delay runs into the A/B harness so we get significance across a 24h trace sample? need to be sure this isn't trace-cherrypick.

ben: added runs to AB harness: run_ids=[2893,2894,2895]. link: https://redwood.internal/ab?runs=2893,2894. Also attached the harness summary CSV to the s3 path.

ben: TL;DR: elastic-window + token_budget=64 + queue_delay=6ms yields better tail for short latency tier (p99 improvement) at cost of ~3-5% throughput. Kernel-choice oddities remain when KV misses are common; recommend adding warmup-penalty to the kernel cost estimator and re-running kernel selector sims.

carol: filing perf ticket with findings and links. tagging eng-runtime and ops. plan: canary config for dedicated pool, 48h, 10%->50%->100% ramp if metrics OK.

oncall: scheduling canary for 2026-03-20 02:00 UTC. rolling plan: 10% (6h) -> 50 (12h) -> 100 if p99 and throughput within thresholds. will alert on regressions.

alice: ack
dave: +1
ben: launching canary builds now, will post results in #eng-runtime. :rocket:
